terms.gloss: a strongbox, a safe; a chest
evidence: Hor. S. 1.1.67: nummōs contemplor in arcā (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A chest or box of any kind (see chest), and above all the strongbox where money was kept; so, by metonymy, one’s money: arcae nostrae cōnfīditō, count on my purse (Cic. Att. 1.9).

terms.gloss: a cupboard, a closet; one that holds money
terms.comment: A cupboard or closet for food, clothes or money: Cicero speaks of one in a house that held “a fair sum of money and gold” (Clu. 64). Its everyday sense is a cupboard (see cupboard).
Traupman’s word, for a box rented in a bank.

phrases.latin: populus mē sībilat, at mihi plaudō ipse domī, simul ac nummōs contemplor in arcā
phrases.english: the people hiss me, but I applaud myself at home as soon as I gaze at the money in my strongbox

sources: Lewis & Short: arca · Lewis & Short: armarium
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 373, checked against the searchable text of the book (11 November 2026).
